chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you intend for something of the good, do not delay it, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may look upon the servant while he is upon something of the obedience, so He says: 'By My Honour and My Majesty! I will not punish you after it, ever!' And when you intend for an evil, do not do it, for indeed He may look upon the servant while he is upon something of the disobedience, so He says: 'By My Honour and My Majesty! I will not forgive you after it, ever!'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of hastening good deeds and delaying evil ones in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the concept of *al-fawq* (divine inspection) at the moment of intention, linking immediate action to eternal destiny. It reflects the Shia theological emphasis on the gravity of the 'moment of death' or divine gaze, where a single act of obedience or sin can seal one's fate, encouraging believers to seize opportunities for good before they are lost.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘Whenever you intend for anything from the goodness, so do not delay it, for Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Notify upon the servant while he is upon something from the obedience, so He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is Saying: ‘By My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Honour and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Majesty! I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> will not Punish you after it, ever!” And when he intends for an evil, but he does not do it, so sometimes Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Notify upon the servant while he is upon something from the disobedience, so He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is Saying: “By My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Honour and My <sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Majesty! I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> will not Forgive (your sins) for you after it, ever!”’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

When you intend to perform a good deed, do not delay doing it; Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, perhaps finds a servant (of Allah) during a good deed of obedience and He, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, may say, ‘I will never subject you to punishment hereafter.’ If you intend to do an evil deed, you must not do it; perhaps Allah finds a servant during an act of disobedience and may say, “I swear by My Majesty and Glory to never forgive you hereafter.’”
